Custom tools

register authors a spec plus a plain-JS body onto the session page. The engine compiles the body debugger-side (CSP-exempt), proves it with a fixture, then persists it as files. Every later open on that origin re-applies them.

agent-webmcp register $H '<json-tool>' '<js-body>' --yes# {"registered":"<name>","handle":"s_…","persisted":true}
bash

Discovery first

The engine cannot inspect pages. Before any register, bring a discovery bundle from your driver (harness browser tools, snapshot plus eval, trace file, page source). Sufficient:

  • url, title, scoped snapshot, target-subtree excerpts
  • candidate_hooks: window functions, forms, fetch endpoints, plus the full schema for the chosen tool
  • console_errors[], flow_steps[]

Ranked best to worst: live snapshot plus eval plus network, then snapshot plus markdown plus bodies, then trace-derived API shapes. Snapshot or text alone is insufficient — no hooks, no schemas, do not author from it.

Binding order matters. Capture in order:

  1. Viewport width (window.innerWidth) — responsive layouts hide entire UIs below breakpoints.
  2. Responsive variants — query every candidate root; note which layout is live (desktop aside vs mobile panel vs none).
  3. Visibility primitives — rect-based (getBoundingClientRect plus computed style). Never offsetParent: fixed elements always read null.
  4. Only then draft spec plus body: prefer page APIs over DOM, feature-detect, fail naming what moved.

The spec and the body

The spec is the standard shape — no title field:

spec.json
{"name": "priceOf","description": "What it changes plus what it returns.","inputSchema": {  "type": "object",  "properties": { "sku": { "type": "string" } },  "required": ["sku"],  "additionalProperties": false},"fixtureInput": { "sku": "demo-1" }}
json

Optional keys: annotations, fixtureInput, strict, consequential. Names match ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$. Duplicates, empty names, empty descriptions, non-object schemas, and empty bodies fail pre-dial.

The body is a plain-JS function expression. No imports, no Effect, no eval, no driver idioms. Five rules for strong tools:

  • Describe effects, not hopes — what it changes plus what it returns.
  • Closed schemas — additionalProperties: false with a real required[].
  • Always include fixtureInput — a tool without one is a rumor (consequential tools excepted: hand-prove those, never auto-run).
  • Verify effects, not echoes — read back the changed state; never trust {saved: true}.
  • Mark consequential tools — consequential: true needs host confirmation; readOnlyHint never bypasses it.

Proving and persistence

Registration succeeding proves nothing — one fixture invoke proves. For stateful tools, prove both transitions (closed→open and open→open): fixtures that pass on one branch are luck, not coverage. For chat-like widgets, gate the fixture read on a settled signal (the reply landed, the typing indicator cleared) — an early read asserts against a loading skeleton.

# variant handling: probe every candidate root,# record which layout answered, fail loud otherwiseagent-webmcp register $H \  '{"name":"chatSend","description":"Send a chat message    and return the settled reply text.",    "inputSchema":{"type":"object","properties":      {"text":{"type":"string"}},"required":["text"],      "additionalProperties":false},    "fixtureInput":{"text":"hello"}}' \  '(async ({ text }) => { … })' --yes
bash

A failed fixture rolls back the live tool and persists nothing: fixture failed (…) — tool rolled back, nothing persisted. Consequential tools skip auto-proof entirely — hand-prove those.

Every success persists to <root>/<origin-slug>/<name>/{spec.json,body.js}. Next open on that origin re-applies them (reapplied[] in the output). Collisions lose loudly to page-native tools; refused tools land in skipped[] with reasons, files kept. list marks live authored tools (authored: true, file age, staleSuspect when a call rotted).

Rot and recovery

Pages move under you. execute failures that smell like rot mark the tool staleSuspect (visible in list): the page refused at runtime, or the tool vanished from the live tool list. Recovery is re-register: refresh discovery, author again, the new files overwrite the old.

agent-webmcp unregister $H <name> --yes   # live onlyrm -r <root>/<origin-slug>/<name>         # files stay# …until you delete them. Deletion is rm, your call.
bash

unregister refuses page-native tools — only session-authored names unregister. Dropping the live tool never deletes the files; close drops everything live but the library outlives the page.
